extracted.intended_audience: newspaper editors, journalists, and press professionals
extracted.subtask_description: Principles and operating standards for voluntary wartime censorship as presented by the Office of Censorship (Byron Price) to newspaper editors; focuses on what censorship may request, what it must avoid, and how it should behave. Applicable to press organizations and government press-censorship bodies during wartime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limited to war security
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary censorship must deal only with war questions involving war security. "If the subject matter does not relate to the war, it is not the business of censorship."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as the Office of Censorship's primary conclusion; voluntary censorship is an unfinished experiment and should confine itself to matters that affect military/security interests rather than general news or opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests must be based on real security danger
rubrics_metrics.description: It must never base a request on any security consideration which may be questionable; the danger to security must be real.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Censorship requests should be grounded in genuine, demonstrable risks to operations or security—not hypothetical or weakly justified concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid interference with editorial opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: It must avoid interference with editorial opinion; such opinion could not possibly be controlled on a voluntary basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Censoring or attempting to control editorial judgments is inappropriate for voluntary press censorship and impractical to sustain; requests should not impinge on editorial voice or viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not withhold information from the American public
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of censorship must be to keep information from the enemy and not from the American people; on no account must it withhold from the public any information that does not damage security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Censorship should make every effort to avoid suppressing legitimate public information; withholding non-sensitive information undermines public confidence and fosters unwarranted suspicion toward government and press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid multiple/duplicative censorship
rubrics_metrics.description: It must make every effort to avoid multiple censorship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate so that overlapping censorship bodies do not create redundant or conflicting controls; multiplicity of censors can cause confusion and unnecessary suppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must not regulate newspaper ethics or release schedules
rubrics_metrics.description: It must never undertake to regulate release dates or other matters of newspaper ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attempting to control publication timing or other ethical/editorial practices would invite deeper government interference and is beyond the remit of voluntary wartime security censorship.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must not vouch for truth or accuracy of news stories
rubrics_metrics.description: It must never undertake to vouch for the truth or accuracy of any news story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Censors should not act as arbiters or guarantors of factual accuracy; doing so leads to embarrassment and inappropriate responsibility for the press's content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and consistency; no favoritism
rubrics_metrics.description: It must be impartial and consistent. 'If any censor is to maintain a position of influence, his blue pencil must know no brother.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Censorship decisions and requests should be applied uniformly without favoritism, personal bias, or special treatment for associates; maintain consistent standards to preserve legitimacy.
